subject: Cloud Computing
title: Custom Hardware at Scale
description: A fast breakdown of Custom Hardware at Scale for builders.

hook.text: Google, Amazon, and Microsoft don't buy servers from Dell. They design and build their own.

buildup.text: At cloud scale, even tiny efficiency gains across millions of servers save billions of dollars.

discovery.text: Google designs custom chips like TPUs for AI. Amazon built Graviton processors for general computing.

twist.text: These custom chips aren't sold to anyone else. They're a competitive weapon, not a product.

climax.text: The cloud giants now rival Intel and AMD as chip innovators — a shift nobody predicted.

punchline.text: Cloud providers don't just rent computers. They reinvent them.

quiz.question: Why do major cloud providers design their own custom chips?
options: Small efficiency gains at massive scale save billions of dollars
Commercial chips are not powerful enough for any cloud workload
Government regulations require custom hardware for cloud use

details.summary: Major cloud providers design custom hardware optimized for their specific workloads rather than buying off-the-shelf servers. AWS builds custom Graviton processors and Nitro cards, Google designs TPUs for AI, and all three design custom networking equipment for maximum efficiency.
details.whyItMatters: Custom hardware gives cloud providers performance and efficiency advantages that are impossible to replicate on standard equipment, making cloud more cost-effective than building your own data center.
takeaways: AWS designs Graviton ARM processors for cloud workloads
Google builds TPUs specifically for AI training and inference
Custom networking equipment handles massive internal traffic

faq.question: Why do cloud providers build custom chips?
faq.answer: At cloud scale, even small efficiency improvements in custom hardware save millions of dollars and reduce power consumption. Custom processors can be optimized for specific workloads like web serving, machine learning, or video encoding in ways general-purpose CPUs cannot match.

faq.question: What is AWS Graviton?
faq.answer: Graviton is AWS's custom ARM-based processor family designed for cloud workloads. Graviton instances offer better price-performance than equivalent Intel instances for many workloads. Graviton3 provides up to 25 percent better compute performance than Graviton2.
